newsitem.title: USA: Georgia urged to use private debt collectors.
newsitem.headline: Georgia urged to use private debt collectors.

text.p: Georgia Revenue Department is owed $541 million in overdue and largely uncollectable tax bills, but could collect about $30 million of that over the next five years by using private debt collectors, a report by KPMG Peat Marwick found.

The recommendation to hire a private tax collector, which would cost about $4.6 million over five years, is part Peat Marwick's 245-page preliminary report on modernizing the revenue department, which collects more than $10 billion annually in taxes and fees.

The report said the state needs to spend at least $90 million over the next five years to bring the department into the electronic age. But it said the state stands to recover most of the investment and save an additional $80 million by 2002 by modernizing.
"No other agency in state government offers such a potential return," Mike Walsh, head of the Peat Marwick team, told the Atlanta Journal and Constitution.

The revenue department was criticized last summer when the state auditor discovered it had guessed how much sales tax revenue to distribute to cities and counties because it could not track actual collections by jurisdiction. The department blamed its outdated computer system.
The over- and under-payments are to be addressed in a pending report.
